The unstable Activity element is no longer an alias for the Offscreen element. It now has its own global React symbol and fiber work tag, while delegating its child rendering to Offscreen behavior. Server rendering recognizes it through the existing Offscreen path, and component naming/DevTools now expose it as "Activity".

[inference, not verified] The exported Activity identity changes from react.offscreen to react.activity. If supported consumers compare, cache, serialize, or manually construct the former symbol—or pair this client export with a renderer that does not recognize the new symbol—Activity elements can cease to be interpreted as they were previously.

[inference, not verified] Client reconciliation introduces a distinct Activity wrapper around an Offscreen fiber, whereas server rendering directly shares Offscreen handling. Hydration and ref behavior should be checked to ensure that this intentionally different internal tree shape remains semantically equivalent.

[inference, not verified] DevTools correctness now depends on mapping numeric work tag 31 to Activity for the appropriate renderer versions; an incorrect version cutoff could cause Activity fibers to be unknown, mislabeled, or filtered inconsistently.
The supplied context does not show which product builds or package entry points actually expose and consume ReactClient's unstable_Activity export.
Observable application impact depends on whether an application renders unstable_Activity and which mode, children, update sequence, and ref usage it supplies.

The supported behavior for mixed versions of React, the reconciler, server renderer, and DevTools is not shown, so compatibility with producers or consumers that only know react.offscreen cannot be established.
The diff does not show the protocol or integration boundary through which DevTools obtains renderer versions and numeric work tags, so the practical coverage of the new tag mapping is unknown.
The accepted values and intended semantics of Activity's mode prop are not included, so equivalence to existing Offscreen modes and behavior cannot be fully established.
